Order 
These appeals arising out of the common award dated 04.01.2012 in Claim Case Nos.01/2010 and 02/2010 passed by I Member MACT Ratlam are heard analogously and disposed off by this common order.
2. M.A.Nos.344/2012 and 708/2015 have been filed by the claimants-Babulal and Ambaram for enhancement of the award amount.
M.A.Nos.678/2012 and 679/2012 have been filed by the owner and driver.

3. The facts of the case are that on 26.08.2007 at about 9 A.M claimants- Ambaram and Babulal were going on motorcycle bearing registration no.MP-43-MA-7228 to Alot and when they reached nearby the hall of Rajesh Parmar, an Eicher Truck bearing registration no.MP-09-GE- 2106 driven by the driver rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle of the claimants due to which they suffered grievous injuries resulting in permanent disability.

4. Learned counsel for the owner and driver has submitted that the learned Claims Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company and saddled the liability on the owner and driver on the ground that the offending vehicle NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8725 3 MA-344-2012 bearing registration no.MP-09-GE-2106 was a transport vehicle being driven by the driver having driving license of only LMV, but in the light of the judgments passed by the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental insurance Company Limited AIR 2017 SC 3668 and Bajaj Allianz Vs. Rambha Devi 2024 ACJ 2623 wherein it has been held that if particular class of vehicle is driven with different type of license, then Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from liability to pay compensation.

5. Learned counsel for the claimants submit that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.
He further submits that the claimants suffered grievous injuries particularly fracture of femur and tibia fibula bone, but that has not been taken into consideration.
On this submission prays for enhancement of the award amount looking to the injuries and consequential permanent disability.

6. Heard and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
In the case of Mukund Dewangan (Surpa) in para 46 it has been observed that in one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.

Relevant para 46 can be beneficially reproduced which runs as under:-

sentences.text: Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.
In one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.

As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8725 4 MA-344-2012 vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre-amended position as well the post- amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the definition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of 'light motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act 'Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle, medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)
(e) to (h) and our conclusion is fortified by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed.

Thus we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
(i) 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.

(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg. would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight"
of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)
(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h)
with expression 'transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid Sabir And Anr. vs Ambaram And 3 Ors. on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69184181/
3 substituted classes only. It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d)
and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

sentences.text:
(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8725 5 MA-344-2012 vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
8.

From bare perusal of the aforesaid elucidation by the Apex Court, it is apparent that if vehicle is LMV, i.e. unladen weight is not more than 7500 kg, it can be driven by the person having license to drive LMV.

In the instant case, undisputedly, the offending vehicle Eicher Truck bearing registration no.MP-09-GE-2106 was LMV as its unladen weight is less than 7500 Kg, therefore, it cannot be said that the respondent/driver was not entitled to drive the aforesaid vehicle with license he has.

Thus,
it is apparent that the learned Claims Tribunal has committed error in holding that there was breach of license and therefore, Insurance Company was not liable to pay compensation.

9. In light of the aforesaid the appeals filed by the owner and driver M.A.No.678/2012 and M.A.No.679/2012 are allowed to the extent that the finding given by the Claims Tribunal exonerating the Insurance Company is not proper, therefore, the aforesaid finding is set aside by holding that Insurance Company is liable for payment of compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

10. Without going into the nicety of the computation and looking to the injuries suffered by the claimants/appellants in M.A.No.344/2012 and M.A.No.708/2015, this Court is of the considered view that if a lump sum amount of Rs.80,000/- for injured Babulal in M.A.No.344/2012 and Rs.40,000/- for injured Ambaram in M.A.No.708/2015 are enhanced that will be just and proper compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8725 6 MA-344-2012 11.

Accordingly, M.A.No.344/2012 and M.A.No.708/2015 are partly allowed by enhancing the compensation by Rs.80,000/- and Rs.40,000/- respectively over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award including interest shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate.
12. Since the Insurance Company has been held liable for payment of compensation, if any amount is deposited by the owner, the same be refunded, in accordance with law.
Let a copy of this order be kept in the connected appeals.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ Sabir And Anr. vs Ambaram And 3 Ors. on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69184181/
